kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reports that NVIDIA has stepped in and begun providing take-or-pay minimum revenue guarantees ("backstops") to Neoclouds for GPU capacity, typically on six-year terms, under which NVIDIA stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels and shares in a portion of the Neocloud's revenue earned above the backstop level; it says NVIDIA has also started backstopping datacenter leases.
passages: This is why Nvidia has stepped in and has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes themselves . In the backstop program, Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment to Neoclouds – a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity. In exchange for this backstop, Nvidia also shares in a portion of the Neocloud’s revenue earned above the backstop level.
Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period.
Here, Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases.

kept_from_that_article.summary: In June 2026 SharonAI announced a 72MW AI factory in Australia, scaling to as many as 40,000 GB300 GPUs under a six-year NVIDIA backstop, and disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B (an implied floor of about $2.33/hr/GPU on average over the six years); SharonAI's footprint is set to grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted, and it guides to more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total by mid-2027.

passages: Nvidia 's next marquee product — the Kyber rack-scale architecture designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips — has been delayed by more than 12 months to 2028, according to research firm SemiAnalysis, the latest in a string of reported setbacks raising questions about the AI giant's product roadmap.
The setback stems from difficulties manufacturing a key circuit board at the heart of the system, SemiAnalysis said in a post on Monday.

"Kyber NVL144 rack architecture has been delayed to 2028 as the PCB midplane remains challenging from a manufacturability standpoint," the firm said, referring to a specialized, multi-layer printed circuit board that connects electronic modules within a system.
NVL576 — a larger system linking eight racks via optical connections — is also likely delayed or limited to small volumes, the research firm said.
